relevance_note: Single-family case report of an infant with LAD1 and a homozygous ITGB2 variant: 'identified a novel in-frame deletion in exon 7 (ITGB2 c.844_846delAAC, p.Asn282del) in the patient'.
method_note: Hand extraction, built with a small Python script in scratch; every span checked verbatim by script. In scope: proband III.3, affected deceased brother III.2 (not genetically tested; no variant row) and the two parents (tested, heterozygous; sex not stated, so labelled 'parent of III.3' and 'parent of III.3 2'). The healthy older brother III.1 (aged 4, HLA-typed only, not tested for the variant, unaffected) was left out as neither tested nor affected. Proband inheritance recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because both parents (sex not stated) carry the variant; the enum has no biparental option. Parents' variant type, pathogenicity and functional evidence left 'not reported' (statements are about the proband's variant). Consanguinity recorded only for the proband (sentence names 'The patient'); ethnicity for relatives taken from 'a Mauritanian family'. Age 'five-month-old' recorded as age at last evaluation (presentation/report); no explicit age at diagnosis. Weight 6550 g (-2 SD) not recorded as a feature (not called abnormal); failure to thrive left not reported. Normal-finding exclusions per D-27; the normal radiological check is recorded as written ('radiological abnormalities') and excludes nothing more specific. Absence of 'cutaneous ulceration' at admission examination used to exclude the necrotic skin ulcer checklist item. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: Figure 3 legend calls the variant a 'novel missense mutation' while the text calls it an in-frame/nonframeshift deletion (in-frame indel recorded); Conclusions print the transcript as 'NM_ 0000211.5' vs 'NM_000211.5' in Table 1 (Table 1 used); Introduction spells the gene 'ITBG2'; Discussion gives CD11/CD18 expression 'less than 2%' vs 1.51% CD18 in Results; basophil and monocyte absolute counts in the blood count are internally inconsistent (not extracted).
